title: One clock-phase step
statement: Let $B$ be a six-tape timed-interpreter configuration on a Boolean input word, let $q,q'$ be timed control states, let $b$ be a Boolean word, let $p$ be an integer, and let $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose that for every scanned input symbol and every tuple of work-tape reads whose clock-tape read is the symbol stored at position $p$ of the buffer tape for $b$, the transition in control $q$ is the administrative action that enters $q'$, moves the clock head by $d$, and makes no write or output. Then one step from the configuration obtained by setting $B$'s control to $q$ and its clock lane to the buffer tape for $b$ with head at $p$ equals the configuration obtained by setting that control to $q'$ and moving the clock head to $p+d$, with the other fields retained.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a configuration of the six-tape timed interpreter on a Boolean input word
for every input read and work-tape read tuple with clock read equal to the buffer-tape content at $p$, the transition in state $q$ is the stated administrative clock move to $q'$

Suppose that, whenever the clock lane reads its designated symbol, the timed
interpreter's transition in control $q$ is a pure clock move by
